category_title: Child with ASD, ADHD, and Specific Learning Disability exhibiting significant behavioral resistance to reading instruction
minimal_context: Sam is working one-on-one with an interventionist to sound out words on treasure hunt clues to find a prize.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Here is the first clue for our treasure hunt. Let's sound out these words to find out where the prize is.

STUDENT: (Gets out of his chair and begins roaming the classroom instead of looking at the clue.)

TUTOR: Please come back to your seat and look at the paper.

STUDENT: No! I don't want to read it.

TUTOR: We need to read the sentence to get the next clue.

STUDENT: (Throws the clue on the floor and begins having a meltdown, screaming and completely refusing to participate in the instructional task.)

options.A: Fade out external reinforcements over time while continuing verbal praise that is specific for good reading.
options.B: Continuously remind the student that he is expected to show he is participating in the reading task, even if he is uncomfortable.
options.C: Encourage the student to bring in items from home that he considers special to keep in an important bag.
options.D: Treat the student's avoidance strategies as compensations rather than active refusals to comply with the reading task.
